mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 0.5% indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS below 0.5% but 5-day forward returns negative in >60% of cases over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate falling below 6.0% signals tightening labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: UNRATE < 6.0% but 20-day forward returns negative in >60% of cases over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in residential sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicate strong consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days through earnings momentum.
failure_condition: RSAFS and HOUST both rise but 60-day forward returns negative in >60% of cases over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 2.5%) increase real discount rates, causing short-term S&P 500 underperformance over 5 days due to reduced equity valuation multiples.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS > 2.5% but 5-day forward returns positive in >60% of cases over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production (INDPRO) reflects robust manufacturing activity that supports corporate profit growth, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: INDPRO rises but 20-day forward returns negative in >60% of cases over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Annual CPI inflation exceeding 2.5% signals persistent price pressures that trigger anticipated monetary tightening, reducing equity valuations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL > 2.5% but 60-day forward returns positive in >60% of cases over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent growth in employment (PAYEMS) and decline in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates accelerating labor market strength that boosts consumer confidence and drives positive 5-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: PAYEMS rises and UNRATE falls but 5-day forward returns negative in >60% of cases over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production below 100 (2017=100) indicates manufacturing contraction, reducing corporate earnings visibility and causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 100 but 20-day forward returns positive in >60% of cases over any 3-year rolling window.
